Will an EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max run an RV rooftop air conditioner? (EU 230 V)

Exceeds output — nothing to time — it will not run see why below ↓

It is the start, not the running. This load demands 8,619 W for the moment it starts, against a 4,800 W surge ceiling — 180% of it. Running draw is only 1,690 W, which is why the watt figure alone would have said yes.

0 – 8,619 W across the rails above

Two numbers decide this, and readers use them interchangeably: watts are the ceiling on what the inverter holds at any instant, watt-hours are how much energy the battery holds. A machine can have plenty of one and not enough of the other.

The verdict is a calculation, not a lookup. What it will not do is print a runtime, and the reason is specific: there is nothing to time. A runtime for a load this machine will not start is a figure about nothing.

Where those numbers come from

A blank is never left blank. A field we have found no figure for says so, and a field whose sources disagree — two documents, or one document with itself — says that instead of picking one.

No usable-capacity figure for this machine

EcoFlow states a nameplate watt-hour number for it, and we have found no published depth of discharge or inverter efficiency for the EU 230 V build. Dividing the nameplate by this load would be wrong by 20–35% in the flattering direction, so this page shows the nameplate for what it is and refuses to turn it into hours.

Missing: station.usable_capacity_wh

Energy rate instead of a runtime

1,690 Wh per hour while it is actually running

This number needs no battery figure at all, which is why this page can give it when it cannot give hours. Divide any usable-capacity figure you trust by it and you have your own runtime, with our arithmetic visible instead of hidden.

What an RV rooftop air conditioner demands

Running power 1,690 W Official spec · verified 2026-08-01 · high confidence
Start-up demand 8,400 W Official spec · verified 2026-08-01 · high confidence

The engine checked 8,619 W — where a record publishes both an absolute inrush and a multiple of running power, the more demanding of the two is used rather than the flattering one.

Start-up duration 200 ms Official spec · verified 2026-08-01 · medium confidence
Power factor 0.95 Official spec · verified 2026-08-01 · medium confidence

The inverter is loaded to 1,779 VA — 1,690 W ÷ 0.95 — which is the quantity its ceiling is actually measured against.

Start-up figure Manufacturer nameplate (locked-rotor)

The start-up figure is the manufacturer’s own locked-rotor rating, off a spec sheet for a real model in this class — not a category multiple. Where a standards table and the nameplate disagree, this library uses the nameplate: the standards figure is a selection envelope for breakers and controllers, and sizing a battery to it over-specifies the machine by two to four times.

What changes the answer

Each row below is the same calculation with one input changed, run again — not the verdict above adjusted by hand. The headline verdict is the machine and the load as they come, because that is what a reader who has not bought an accessory needs first.

With a soft starter fitted Runs it

A soft starter ramps the motor instead of connecting it straight to the line. Two vendors publish reductions of 70% and “up to 75%”; this site models the conservative end, 70%, floored at the running draw. That takes the start-up demand from 8,619 W to 2,586 W — and it changes the answer. The verdict at the top of this page is the machine as it comes, because that is what a reader who has not bought an accessory needs to see first.

What this page is not going to sell you

There is no buy button on this page, and that is the finding rather than an omission: the EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max does not run an RV rooftop air conditioner. A price here would be a sale, not an answer.

Questions people ask about this pairing

Will an EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max run an RV rooftop air conditioner?
No. The binding constraint is the surge ceiling: 8,619 W demanded at start-up against a 4,800 W ceiling. That is a calculation against this machine's own record, not a lookup. Nothing in our library clears this load, which is itself the answer.
How long will an EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max run an RV rooftop air conditioner?
It does not, so there are no hours to give. That is why the panel at the top shows an em dash rather than a number: a runtime for a load the machine cannot start is a figure about nothing.
Would a soft starter let an EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max run an RV rooftop air conditioner?
A soft starter ramps the motor instead of connecting it straight to the line. Two vendors publish reductions of 70% and “up to 75%”; this site models the conservative end, 70%, floored at the running draw. That takes the start-up demand from 8,619 W to 2,586 W — and it changes the answer. The verdict at the top of this page is the machine as it comes, because that is what a reader who has not bought an accessory needs to see first. Under that condition the verdict is “Runs it”. Both runs are on this page because a conclusion that depends on a condition is only honest when the condition is named.
